sources.title: SEC Form 8-K (August 17, 2026) — NVIDIA Corp.
claims: According to NVIDIA's SEC Form 8-K filing, the company entered into residual-value guarantees with SB Energy for leases of approximately 4.25 gigawatts of IT load, with an aggregate payment obligation capped at $105 billion.
The finalized transaction is documented in NVIDIA's SEC Form 8-K filing, which outlines the residual-value guarantees for up to 4.25 gigawatts of IT load developed by SoftBank's SB Energy subsidiary.
Under this agreement, NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation is capped at $105 billion.
sources.quote: On August 17, 2026, NVIDIA entered into multiple residual value guaranties (collectively, the “Agreements”) with SB Energy (the “Lessor”) relating to leases for approximately 4.25 gigawatts of IT load in the aggregate at the Portsmouth Site. ... NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation is cumulatively capped at $105 billion for its initial commitment under the Agreements.
sources.reason: The SEC Form 8-K filing confirms that NVIDIA entered into residual value guarantees with SB Energy for leases of approximately 4.25 gigawatts of IT load, with an aggregate payment obligation capped at $105 billion.

sources.title: NVIDIA Circular Financing Allegations — TechPowerUp
claims: This circular loop is detailed in reports from outlets like TechPowerUp, which highlight how these mechanisms kept hardware prices artificially high.
sources.quote: alleging that NVIDIA artificially inflated the ongoing GPU and memory shortage by investing in AI startups that would go on to buy NVIDIA GPUs and build data centers.
sources.reason: The source confirms that NVIDIA allegedly engineered scarcity and artificially inflated the GPU and memory shortage through circular financing of AI startups.

sources.title: Colette Kress vs Jensen Huang Rift — Times of India
claims: According to reports published by The Times of India, Huang cut off Kress mid-presentation, calling her a reporting CFO who was acting like a deer in the headlights when she urged caution regarding the company's ballooning credit guarantees.
Kress was highly concerned about a proposed $250 billion financial backstop for OpenAI's data center campus, successfully fighting to scale back the signed guarantee cap to a maximum of $120 billion.
This boardroom conflict with CFO Colette Kress, combined with personal governance challenges, led to his immediate departure as documented in reports by The Times of India.
sources.quote: Huang interrupted Kress during her presentation, according to a person familiar with his remarks cited by The Wall Street Journal. He later called her a “reporting CFO”, suggesting she could report the numbers but was not equipped to help him shape strategy or make decisions.
sources.reason: The source confirms the confrontation between Huang and Kress, the reduction of the OpenAI backstop from $250B to $120B, and Huang's departure following personal relationship revelations.

sources.title: NVIDIA Circular Financing Report — Lavx
claims: According to reports from Lavx, this strategy of circular financing allowed the chipmaker to maintain high GPU demand and keep hardware pricing artificially elevated.
sources.quote: The report claims NVIDIA used these investments to keep demand for its chips high while it moved an oversupply of semiconductors from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. The report frames the strategy as circular financing: NVIDIA funds customers, and those customers buy NVIDIA hardware.
sources.reason: The article confirms that NVIDIA used circular financing to keep GPU demand high, which shaped supply and demand signals in a market with higher prices.

sources.title: NVIDIA Controversy and GPU Pricing — RV Visual Craft
claims: This has forced local firms to navigate a steep 18% goods and services tax alongside premium retail pricing on consumer GPUs.
According to market analyses by RV Visual Craft, the retail price of consumer graphics cards in India has been artificially inflated due to limited local stock allocations.
For instance, a high-end consumer GPU with a US MSRP of $1,999 converts to approximately ₹1,68,915 at an exchange rate of ₹84.50 per USD.
sources.quote: Indian retail pricing includes the standard 18% GST plus import duties and local distributor margins.
sources.reason: The source confirms the 18% GST, the artificial supply constraints/stock rationing causing inflated retail prices in India, and the $1,999 US MSRP for a flagship consumer GPU.

sources.title: NVIDIA $530B Commitments and Guarantees — Dev.to
claims: NVIDIA expanded its total outstanding commitments and guarantees to $530.5 billion to prop up demand for its GPUs.
The total commitments and guarantees ballooned from $184 billion to $530.5 billion in a single quarter, reflecting a concerted effort to underwrite the artificial intelligence infrastructure market.
A substantial portion of this, specifically $279 billion, represents direct supply commitments for memory and chip wafers, while another $36 billion is allocated to buy back unused cloud capacity.
sources.quote: Nvidia's total commitments and guarantees reached about $530 billion last quarter — up from $184 billion the quarter before, a near-tripling in three months. ... $279 billion of that is supply commitments for memory and chip wafers ... $36 billion is locked in deals to buy back unused cloud capacity
sources.reason: The source confirms the commitments ballooned from $184 billion to about $530 billion, with $279 billion for supply commitments and $36 billion to buy back unused cloud capacity.
